action.summary: The sum of the elements of the $m$th row is simply \[\sum_{i=0}^{m} \binom{m}{i} = \sum_{i=0}^m \binom{m}{i}1^i = (1+1)^m=2^m\] by the binomial theorem.

source.problem: For each integer $n$, let $f(n)$ be the sum of the elements of the $n$th row (i.e. the row with $n+1$ elements) of Pascal's triangle minus the sum of all the elements from previous rows. For example, \[f(2) = \underbrace{(1 + 2 + 1)}_{\text{2nd row}} - \underbrace{(1 + 1 + 1)}_{\text{0th and 1st rows}} = 1. \]What is the minimum value of $f(n)$ for $n \ge 2015$?
